newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen rangebound watching U.S..
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen rangebound watching U.S..

text.p: Belgian shares, which spent a quiet day in negative territory on Friday, are expected to remain rangebound for much of the next two weeks in the run up to the November 5 U.S. presidential elections, traders said.
"The markets will be watching the U.S. for the next fortnight, although the result looks like a foregone conclusion," one trader said.

Traders also noted that German Bundesbank Council member Otmar Issing was keeping the money markets on their toes with seemingly contradictory remarks on the possibility of further interest rate cuts. This in turn was effecting share markets.
Issing, who earlier this week seemed to rule out further cuts in German interest rates, on Friday in Brussels told reporters a cut was not totally out of the question.
Traders noted that for the second successive day the volume of business on the Brussels bourse was well below average with buyers and sellers both sidelined waiting for a signal to move.
The total value of business on the bourse was just 1.6 billion francs on Friday after Thursday's 1.4 billion francs.
A good average day on the bourse is around 2.5 billion francs. The Bel-20 share index ended 1.11 points down at 1,810.07 in a 1,810.28/1,800.58 range.
Spector was the main focus as the film finisher's scrip issue went to market and traders piled in to buy it and sell the shares to take an arbitrage profit.
Holding nine scrips entitles the owner to buy four shares at a pre-set price 1,865 francs each.
"You have the calculation in your computer and it tells you exactly what the underlying value of the scrip is. It is easy. Everyone has been doing it," one trader said.
Spector ended the day 2.2 percent down at 1,985 francs. The scrip was quoted at 10 francs.
